text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime streaming-api-prod p99 latency spike detected — current p99 2.12s (SLO 0.9s). Spike start ~2865412200. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/streaming-prod?from=now-30m

alice (oncall): acknowledged. paging SRE. I'm oncall — will triage. @ben can you take the lead on infra checks?

ben (eng-sre): on it. first quick checks: KV cache hitrate, host CPU/mem, recent deploys, and network error rates. running queries now.

ben (eng-sre): grafana snippet: `sum(rate(kv_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_requests[5m])) * 100` => dropped from ~98% to ~63% starting +9m.

carmen (prodeng): deploy-bot just posted a release ~9m ago. deploy-bot: Released streaming-service@v2.14.1 by carmen — commit abc123 — 2865412100.

devon (customer-ops): seeing a rise in stalled streaming sessions in EU-west region too — session connect timeouts and stalled frames. Roughly ~120 affected sessions in last 10m, mostly SDK v1.8 clients.

ben (eng-sre): logs show repeated `kvcache: miss -> backend fetch` and increased backend tail latency. Also saw a few `OOMKill` events on pod streaming-worker-3. Pasting relevant log excerpt:
```
Mar 17 12:34:21 streaming-worker-3 kubelet: Pod killed: OOMKilled, container streams-handler
Mar 17 12:34:22 streams-handler[pid]: fetch backend latency=1.1s seq=... id=...
```

alice (oncall): to reduce customer impact quickly: 1) shift a small percentage of traffic to fallback CPU-backed pool (lower throughput, stable tail latency) 2) scale up streaming-worker pool by +3 replicas (temp) 3) enable knob `streaming.slowpath_throttle=true` to limit new long-lived sessions. Carmen can we flip route fallback and scale? Ben, can you check autoscaler/limits?

carmen (prodeng): flipping route fallback now to 5% canary. running: `rbacctl route set streaming-api-prod --fallback cpu-small --weight 5`

carmen (prodeng): scaling up replicas: `k scale deployment/streaming-worker --replicas=12 -n prod` — executed.

ben (eng-sre): autoscaler config shows max surge already at 12 so manual scale applied. I patched HPA min temporarily to avoid reversion. Also increased node pool by +2 nodes (provisioning).

ben (eng-sre): after initial canary shift p99 dropped to 1.05s in canary buckets. Global p99 moving down to ~1.4s. KV hitrate still low but backend tail reduced after scale.

devon (customer-ops): starting outbound support message draft. ETA request from customers?

eva (support): holding draft: "We’re seeing intermittent streaming stalls affecting a subset of sessions; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15 minutes with next steps." Any specific guidance for high-value customers?

alice (oncall): temp mitigation steps executed. monitoring for 15m. If stable, we'll broaden fallback to 30% and keep scaled capacity while we root-cause. Ben — next: correlate v2.14.1 changes to kvcache behavior and check memory usage in new image.

ben (eng-sre): already diffing image layers. Early suspicion: cache warming logic changed and increases mem pressure on worker leading to evictions. Opening debug job to reproduce with load.

carmen (prodeng): rolling back is an option if we see regression persist after 15m. Standby for rollback playbook.

alice (oncall): thanks. current plan: 15m watch, escalate to rollback if p99 > 1.2s or error rate rises. @everyone — react with :eyes: when you’ve seen this thread.

ben (eng-sre): marking this thread as active mitigation. monitoring graphs: p95 -> 0.35s, p99 -> 1.1s in canary after route shift.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty page created — PD-INC-4821 assigned to alice.

alice (oncall): updating support and customers in 10m. I'll post follow-up here.

ben (eng-sre): follow-up: memory profile shows an extra ~150MB per connection in new binary at high concurrency; working on hotfix branch to revert change.

alice (oncall): closing mitigation loop for now — traffic fallback and scale holding. Will keep monitoring; leave incident open until root cause fix or rollback.

ben (eng-sre): continuing root cause. will update in 20m or on change.

eva (support): posted initial customer note to affected tenants.

alice (oncall): thanks all — good collaboration.
